title: NIST MEP: Manufacturers Guide to Cybersecurity for Small and Medium-Sized Manufacturers

history.reason: Source fetched and read directly on the access date; findings transcribed from the document.

publisher: NIST Manufacturing Extension Partnership (MEP National Network)
reliability: US government (NIST MEP) document; MEP funds and promotes the assistance it describes, so it has an interest in presenting need for that assistance. Contains third-party statistics reproduced in charts; underlying surveys not read.
findings: The guide states: "Because SMMs typically don't have the resources to invest in cybersecurity the way larger manufacturers can, many cyber criminals view them as soft targets."
The guide states SMMs "are often less prepared" to handle a hacker, natural-disaster or resource-loss event, and that "SMMs often see cybersecurity as too difficult or too expensive."

A callout cites the 2017 Ponemon Institute report "State of Cybersecurity in Small & Medium-Sized Businesses": 61% of small businesses experienced a cyberattack in the past 12 months (all small businesses, not manufacturers only).

A chart titled "Actions taken to enhance cybersecurity" (source: Sikich M&D Report 2019) shows, as printed, higher percentages for companies with less than $500M revenue than for those with more than $500M on every one of seven actions (e.g., hiring internal cybersecurity professionals 69% vs 37%; partnering with an outside firm 57% vs 42%). The blue/grey legend assignment is as read from the rendered page.
The guide says SMMs may be able to detect and recover quickly because they often have less complex operational needs and IT infrastructure.
limitations: PDF metadata creation date is October 2019; the document carries no printed publication date, so published is recorded as null.
Qualitative assertions are not accompanied by NIST-measured data; the third-party statistics were not traced to their original surveys.

The chart population (companies by revenue, not manufacturers specifically; $500M threshold is far above SMM size) is unclear and appears to contradict the guide's narrative; it may be mislabeled or unrepresentative.
